title: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy
provenance: reported by HappySmurfday (highball#63), Epic copy, unverified by Highball
notes: DirectX 12 only: on DXMT it stops at "No suitable D3D12 adapter found" before the splash, so D3DMetal is the only mode that can run it and this row exists to make Highball ask for Apple's licence at the first launch. With D3DMetal 3.0 the splash renders, then the game crashes after Play Game with Wine's program error dialog: its log shows D3DMetal refusing the two DirectX 12 timestamp-query calls (EndQuery and ResolveQueryData, type 2) and, right after, a read through a null pointer. Apple's D3DMetal does not support timestamp queries and Apple has said so without a timeline. Not fixable at Highball's level today. Reported on an M4 Max on a macOS 27 beta, Epic copy. Not tried here.

requiresLauncher.name: Epic Games Launcher
requiresLauncher.note: Reported with the Epic copy; the Steam copy has not been tried.

knownIssues.symptom: Crashes after "Play Game" on the splash screen, with Wine's "has encountered a serious problem" dialog, on D3DMetal. The AVX toggle makes no difference.
knownIssues.cause: D3DMetal 3.0 does not implement DirectX 12 timestamp queries. The log (highball#63) shows it refusing ID3D12GraphicsCommandList::EndQuery and ResolveQueryData for query type 2 (timestamp), followed by an unhandled page fault reading address 0x907, a null result the game then dereferences. Apple's engineers have acknowledged the missing support on their forums with no timeline (developer.apple.com/forums/thread/757107).
knownIssues.fix: In development: a DirectX 12 through Vulkan mode (vkd3d-proton with DXVK's DXGI over MoltenVK) built and patched for Apple GPUs. On 2026-09-06 it creates a DirectX 12 device on both engines, declares feature level 12_0 and Shader Model 6.6, returns real timestamp queries and presents frames, which is everything this game asked for and D3DMetal could not give. The game itself has not been run through it yet (78 GB of disk). Tracked with highball-db#6.
